title.narrative: Emergency Health Response to Hurricane Beryl

description.narrative: Hurricane Beryl, the first major hurricane of the 2024 season, set records as the earliest Category 5 storm in the North Atlantic. Making landfall as a high-end Category 4 storm in Grenada and St Vincent and the Grenadines, Beryl caused widespread devastation. Carriacou, Petite Martinique, and St. Patrick Parish in Grenada saw nearly total destruction, extensive power outages, and critical water interruptions. In St Vincent and the Grenadines, significant damage to housing and essential services, including many health facilities rendered inoperative due to infrastructural damage and disrupted utilities, has severely limited access to medical care. The destruction of homes and infrastructure has left residents without proper shelter, increasing exposure to environmental hazards and health risks. The lack of potable water and proper sanitation raises the risk of disease outbreaks, including respiratory infections, vector-borne diseases like dengue, and gastroenteritis. Urgent support is needed to address the extensive damage, restore essential services, and reduce health risks for the affected populations.This CERF project aims to mitigate the negative impact of Hurricane Beryl on the health and lives of affected communities by ensuring continued access to and availability of essential health services to the local population as well as protecting individuals in vulnerable situations against arising health threats in the post-hurricane degraded context. To do so, CERF funds will support 1/ the rapid recuperation of operational capacity of impacted health facilities to support continued delivery of critical health services as well as 2/ the intensification of surveillance, risk communication and health promotion interventions in most affected communities to support the early detection and timely management of arising health threats as well as the adoption of protective and preventive good practices to reduce health risks for affected populations. Prioritized activities will include the implementation of urgent rapid repairs in damaged facilities to restore operational capacity and safe conditions, the procurement of critical health supplies and equipment for essential care delivery, intensification of syndromic surveillance interventions in shelters and affected communities, rapid refresher training of health professional on mental health assistance and psychosocial support, GBV assistance, as well as infectious diseases outbreak detection and management, the procurement of rapid diagnostic tests, and the dissemination of risk communication and health education materials to affected communities to raise awareness of health risks and protective measures among community members.
